input.content:
- TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol.
- UDP is a connectionless transport protocol.
- IPv4 addresses are 32 bits long.
- IPv6 addresses are 128 bits long.
- HTTP uses TCP port 80 by default.
- HTTPS uses TCP port 443 by default.
- DNS primarily uses port 53.
- SSH uses TCP port 22 by default.
- The OSI model has seven layers.
- The TCP/IP model has four layers.
- A MAC address is 48 bits long.
- ARP maps IPv4 addresses to MAC addresses.
- IPv6 uses NDP instead of ARP.
- DHCP assigns IP addresses automatically.
- DHCP uses UDP ports 67 and 68.
- TCP opens connections with a three-way handshake.
- The handshake uses SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK.
- TTL limits how many hops a packet can take.
- Traceroute relies on TTL expiry messages.
- Ping uses ICMP echo request and reply.
- 127.0.0.1 is the IPv4 loopback address.
- ::1 is the IPv6 loopback address.
- 10.0.0.0/8 is a private IPv4 range.
- 172.16.0.0/12 is a private IPv4 range.
- 192.168.0.0/16 is a private IPv4 range.
- NAT lets many hosts share one public IP.
- CIDR notation expresses prefix length after a slash.
- A /24 IPv4 subnet holds 256 addresses.
- Ethernet's standard MTU is 1500 bytes.
- BGP routes traffic between autonomous systems.
- BGP runs over TCP port 179.
- OSPF is a link-state routing protocol.
- RIP is a distance-vector routing protocol.
- RIP limits routes to 15 hops.
- A switch forwards frames using MAC addresses.
- A router forwards packets using IP addresses.
- VLANs split one switch into logical networks.
- 802.1Q is the VLAN tagging standard.
- Wi-Fi is defined by the IEEE 802.11 family.
- Ethernet is defined by IEEE 802.3.
- TLS encrypts traffic between client and server.
- TLS 1.3 needs one round trip for a full handshake.
- QUIC runs over UDP.
- HTTP/3 is built on QUIC.
- HTTP/2 multiplexes streams over one connection.
- DNS A records map names to IPv4 addresses.
- DNS AAAA records map names to IPv6 addresses.
- CNAME records alias one name to another.
- MX records point to mail servers.
- SMTP uses port 25 for server relay.
- There are 13 named DNS root server identities.
- Anycast routes to the nearest of many hosts.
- Multicast delivers packets to a group of hosts.
- Broadcast reaches every host on a segment.
- IPv6 has no broadcast addresses.
- TCP uses sliding windows for flow control.
- TCP congestion control adjusts sending rate.
- CUBIC is Linux's default congestion algorithm.
- BBR models bandwidth and round-trip time.
- Latency is the time for data to travel.
- Bandwidth is the maximum data rate of a link.
- Jitter is variation in packet delay.
- Packet loss forces TCP to retransmit.
- A firewall filters traffic by rules.
- Stateful firewalls track connection state.
- VPNs tunnel traffic through encrypted links.
- WireGuard is a modern UDP-based VPN protocol.
- Ports range from 0 to 65535.
- Ports below 1024 are well-known ports.
- A socket is an IP address plus a port.
- Load balancers spread traffic across servers.
- CDNs cache content close to users.
- A proxy forwards requests on a client's behalf.
- A reverse proxy sits in front of servers.
- NTP synchronizes clocks over UDP port 123.
- SNMP is used to monitor network devices.
- Fiber optics carry data as light pulses.
- Cat6 cable supports 10 Gbps over short runs.
- Wireshark captures and inspects packets.
- The internet's precursor was ARPANET.
